Tdoc Quota: Maximum allowed number of Tdocs for any company. This is set by the RAN3 Chairman for submission towards an Agenda Item or Sub-Agenda Item. It is indicated in the Chairman's Notes in the heading of each Agenda Item or Sub-Agenda Item. The quota indicated in an Agenda Item applies to the sum of the Tdocs submitted to all its sub-Agenda Items unless otherwise specified; this is to allow the freedom to prioritize which sub-topics to contribute to. Meeting the Tdoc quota does not guarantee that the Tdocs will be treated. If a sourcing company exceeds its quota for an AI, none of its contributions for that AI will be treated. (This limit is to be taken very seriously. The aim is to limit the available "ammunition", in order for companies to prioritize their "targets" and to make the meeting more efficient.) Response papers count toward the Tdoc quota. The following does not count toward the Tdoc quota: Rapporteur input (TS/TR Rapporteur, WI/SI Rapporteur); Pre-agreed input (BL CR updates, e-mail discussion reports, etc.); Contributions allocated during the meeting (revisions, summaries of offline discussion, draft LSs/reply LSs, etc.); One Draft Reply LS from the contact company of an incoming LS. (This ensures that the spirit of good cooperation in RAN3 stays the same.) Late contributions submitted during the meeting, which do not fall into these 4 categories, count toward the Tdoc quota. Co-signed contributions – If the contribution is signed by 2 companies, it counts toward the Tdoc quota for the first company listed. If it is signed by 3 or more companies, it does not count toward the Tdoc quota for any company. For corrections to previous and current releases (i.e. Cat. F CRs and companion discussion paper submitted to AIs 9.x and 31.x), if there are 2 sourcing companies and at least one of them is an operator, the contribution does not count toward the Tdoc quota for any company. (The above aims to encourage honest cooperation and coordination before the meeting, especially on corrections, e.g. IOT issues and/or issues involving operators, which may act as “gatekeepers” of critical corrections. The Chairman will consider the list of co-signers with this spirit.) All current "RAN3 best practices" and suggestions, including those found in R3-172219, still apply. (In other words, how we conduct meetings does not change. Contributions and presentations are always expected to be short, focused and concise, and it is always up to the Chairman's discretion how to conduct the discussion.)
